record.title: Quang Tri suspends auxiliary gates and local routes on Laos frontier
record.region: East and Southeast Asia and Oceania
record.scope: Quang Tri land frontier with Savannakhet and Salavan; auxiliary gates, trails and river crossing points
record.direction: Both directions across specified local frontier routes.
record.movement: Border residents and other movement through auxiliary routes, initially goods as well as people.
record.exceptions: Goods-only exchange at four gates permitted by 12 May; ordinary passengers remained prohibited.
record.imposing_authority: Quang Tri Border Guard Command; cooperating Lao provincial authorities
record.enforcement: March field report observed guarded trails refusing residents passage; does not establish uniform control of every informal path.
record.relationship: Local precursor to EA014 and related to EA016; distinct province and timing from R3-EA-008/R3-EA-009.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; unknown endpoints are not extended to 21 October 2026.
record.context: Local early restriction predates later national measures.
record.uncertainty: May 12 is publication date of an undated permission, not an actual reopening date. Ordinary-passenger end remains unknown. An August official interview retrospectively gives February 3, while the earlier instrument-specific and May accounts give February 4; preferred day retained with qualification.

historical.duration_note: No supported continuous operational interval for the stated scope.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Order plus field reporting establishes local crossing suspension.
February 4 preferred: March field report cites Decision 259/QD-BCH and May government account agrees. August official interview instead says February 3; exact day remains qualified.
Undated goods relaxation does not end passenger prohibition.

Auxiliary routes; four gates named. Passenger and goods phases differ.
